'''Jean-Claude Lorquet''' (born 19 September 1935) is a professor of [[theoretical chemistry|Theoretical Chemistry]] at the [[University of Liège]]. He is member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science]] and author of over 100 scientific papers.

Some of his students are also well known for their contribution to quantum chemistry and reactivity: [[Michèle Desouter-Lecomte]], [[Bernard Leyh]], [[Françoise Remacle]].

Lorquet was born in [[Liège]], [[Belgium]].

== Important contributions ==
* Theory of [[mass spectrometry|mass spectra]].
* Study of [[reaction coordinate|reaction path]]s and of dissociation mechanisms of electronically excited molecular [[ion]]s.
* [[vibronic coupling|Nonadiabatic interactions]].
* [[Avoided crossing]]s and [[conical intersection]]s.
* Transition probabilities between two coupled [[potential energy surface]]s.
* Statistical calculation of [[rate constant]]s of [[nonadiabatic reactions]].
* Validity of statistical theories of unimolecular reactions under collision-free conditions.
* Study of intramolecular vibrational energy relaxation, of [[phase space]] sampling and of unimolecular laws of [[resonance|decay]] via [[autocorrelation function]]s.
* Occurrence of quantum effects in competitive unimolecular reactions.
